covalent.note: Covalent radius; PubChem's values are those of Cordero et al., Dalton Trans. 2008, 2832.

vdw.note: Van der Waals radius (Los Alamos National Laboratory).

electronAffinity.note: PubChem lists no electron affinity for this element.

allen.note: Configuration energy (Allen electronegativity) in eV, not converted to the Pauling-like scale; Mann 2000a.

crust.note: Jefferson Lab estimate for Earth's crust, via PubChem ('2.33×10⁴ milligrams per kilogram').

ocean.note: Jefferson Lab estimate for sea water, via PubChem ('1.29×10³ milligrams per liter').

solar.note: Proto-solar (4.567 Ga ago) elemental mass fraction, column 'Elemental Mass Fractions' of ESM Table A13; the table gives no uncertainty (relative sigma of N(E) in Table 6 applies).

solarLogEps.note: A(E) = log10(N_E/N_H) + 12, 'Solar System Present' log (E/H)+12; basis: average of solar and meteoritic values; unc = 1 sigma in dex as printed.

body.note: In a 70 kg reference adult (ICRP Publication 23, 1975, Table 110).

crystal.reference: Straumanis, M. E. (1949). Journal of Applied Physics 20, 726.

tonnesPerYear.note: World primary (smelter) production, magnesium metal, 2025 (USGS: 1,100 thousand metric tons).

unitValue.note: Price, annual average: U.S. spot Western, dollars per pound [Magnesium Metal], 2025; per kg of the material named, as USGS gives it.

origin.note: Read off Fig. 39 at the dotted 'age of the Sun' line (t = 9.2 Gyr after the Big Bang, 4.6 Gyr ago): pixel fractions of the stacked areas (agb 0.128, massive_stars 0.867, white_dwarfs 0.005); quantised to 0.05. Stack height 78 px. Paper: 'For the elements from Ne to Ge, the newly synthesized amounts are very small for AGB stars, and the small green areas are mostly for mass loss.' Paper: 'Mg is slightly under-produced in the model.'

air.text: Stable in ordinary air under a thin oxide film; oxidises slowly in moist air and is strongly attacked by salt spray.

water.text: Reacts only slowly with cold water, giving hydrogen; powder reacts faster.

acids.text: Dissolves in most acids with hydrogen given off; hydrofluoric acid leaves it almost untouched.

splitting.note: Splitting measured directly by microwave Ramsey spectroscopy in an RF trap (Brewer et al. 2019). The A quoted is the authors' 'uncorrected' A' = splitting/3, which ignores higher-order hyperfine terms. The older 1981 Penning-trap A' (-596 254 376(54) Hz) lies about 2 sigma lower.

gamma.note: Γ/2π from NIST's A_ki = 4.91e+08 s⁻¹ (accuracy class A), taking the upper level to decay only on this line; where it has other decay channels the true linewidth is slightly larger.

laserCooling.note: first_mot = the paper the Olmschenk catalog lists as first 'laser cooled and trapped'. The paper reports Ramsey spectroscopy on laser cooled and trapped Mg; the isotope is not named in the title. NIST observed value.

gamma.note: Γ/2π from NIST's A_ki = 2.6e+08 s⁻¹ (accuracy class A+), taking the upper level to decay only on this line; where it has other decay channels the true linewidth is slightly larger.

laserCooling.note: Cooled in 1978, the same year as Ba+. first_cooled = the paper the Olmschenk ion catalog lists as first 'trapped/laser cooled'.

plantRole.text: The atom at the centre of chlorophyll; it also binds ATP and holds ribosomes together.

humanRole.text: Needed by hundreds of enzymes, above all those that use ATP, which acts as a magnesium complex.

history.discoveredText: 1755 (recognized as an element; metal first obtained 1808)
history.nameOrigin: From Magnesia, a district of Thessaly in Greece, which gave its name to several minerals.
history.note: PubChem's YearDiscovered (1808) is the year Davy first obtained the metal, in impure form; CIAAW credits Bussy with the pure metal in 1831, which Los Alamos calls the first coherent metal.

prose.text: Magnesium is a light, silvery alkaline-earth metal that burns with a dazzling white flame, once used in photographers' flashes; alloyed, it lightens car and aircraft parts. Its most important place in biology is the centre of every chlorophyll molecule, where a single magnesium ion is gripped by four nitrogen atoms of the surrounding ring; leaves short of magnesium turn yellow between their veins. The atom has the closed configuration [Ne] 3s² (ground term ¹S₀). Of its three stable isotopes, only magnesium-25, about 10 % of the total, has a nuclear spin (5/2); the other two have none.
